title: Fix the unstructured summary
scenario: A teammate needs customer feedback summarized for a product meeting, but wrote a prompt that will produce prose — impossible to scan or paste into the minutes.
task: Rewrite the prompt so the output arrives in a usable shape.
weakPrompt: Summarize the customer feedback for the product meeting.

criteria.label: Names the output structure
criteria.hint: Table, numbered list, three sections — pick one and say it.

criteria.label: Defines the fields or columns
criteria.hint: What goes in each row: theme, frequency, example, priority…

criteria.label: Sets count and length limits
criteria.hint: Rows, words per cell, total length.

criteria.label: Gives the ordering or priority rule
criteria.hint: Sorted by frequency, by severity, grouped by product area…

sampleSolution: Summarize the customer feedback below for a product meeting as a table with columns: theme, frequency (number of mentions), one example quote, suggested priority (high/medium/low). Maximum six rows, sorted by frequency, maximum 15 words per cell. No commentary outside the table.
hints: Where will this text go next — and what shape does that place need?
explanation: The fixed prompt turns “a summary” into a specific artifact: a six-row table with named columns, limits and an ordering rule. Format is a constraint — and stated constraints make weak answers visible at a glance instead of hiding inside good prose.
